# Overview

`regionalpcs` applies principal components analysis separately within each
user-defined genomic region. Each retained component provides a score for each
sample, summarizing a pattern of covariation among that region's CpGs. Regions
can be promoters, gene bodies, enhancers, or other intervals of interest.

The loadings describe each CpG's contribution to a regional PC. CpGs with
opposite loadings contribute in opposite directions, so a regional PC can
capture patterns that are lost when methylation values are averaged.

# Installation

Install the release compatible with your R and Bioconductor versions:

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("regionalpcs")
```

The example below uses simulated M-values. An array-data example is included
at the end of the vignette.

```{r packages}
library(regionalpcs)
library(GenomicRanges)
```

# Input data

The methylation input is a numeric matrix or data frame with CpGs in rows and
samples in columns. CpG row names must be unique. At least two samples are
required. Values must be finite, and probe filtering should be completed before
computing regional PCs. Constant CpGs should be removed; variance fractions are
undefined for a region with no variation.

Beta values are proportions on the 0--1 scale. M-values are log2 ratios of
methylated to unmethylated signal and are on a different scale. The package does
not transform values or standardize each CpG to unit variance. The input scale
therefore affects the scores and the number of components retained.

We simulate three regions with six CpGs each. CpGs within a region share a
sample-level pattern, with independent noise added to each measurement.

```{r simulated-data}
set.seed(2026)
n_samples <- 40L
n_regions <- 3L
cpgs_per_region <- 6L
n_cpgs <- n_regions * cpgs_per_region
region_index <- rep(seq_len(n_regions), each = cpgs_per_region)
latent <- matrix(rnorm(n_regions * n_samples), nrow = n_regions)
mvals <- 2 * latent[region_index, ] +
    matrix(rnorm(n_cpgs * n_samples, sd = 0.3), nrow = n_cpgs)
rownames(mvals) <- paste0("cg", seq_len(n_cpgs))
colnames(mvals) <- paste0("sample", seq_len(n_samples))

cpg_gr <- GRanges(
    seqnames = "chr1",
    ranges = IRanges(start = rep(c(1000, 2000, 3000), each = cpgs_per_region) +
        rep(seq_len(cpgs_per_region), n_regions), width = 1)
)
names(cpg_gr) <- rownames(mvals)
regions_gr <- GRanges(
    seqnames = "chr1",
    ranges = IRanges(start = c(1000, 2000, 3000), width = 100)
)
names(regions_gr) <- c("region-A", "region-B", "region-C")
```

For real genomic inputs, both `GRanges` objects must use the same genome build
and compatible chromosome names. `create_region_map()` does not lift coordinates
between builds. Name the CpG ranges with the same IDs used in the methylation
matrix, and name the region ranges with your intended region IDs.

```{r region-map}
region_map <- create_region_map(cpg_gr, regions_gr)
head(region_map)
```

The first two columns of a region map contain region IDs and CpG IDs,
respectively. Column names are ignored. A map can also be supplied directly:

```{r custom-map}
custom_map <- data.frame(
    region_id = names(regions_gr)[region_index],
    cpg_id = rownames(mvals)
)
```

A CpG can contribute to multiple overlapping regions. Repeated copies of the
same region--CpG pair are also preserved and give that CpG repeated influence;
remove accidental duplicate pairs before analysis. Regions are returned in
first-occurrence order, and CpGs retain their order within each region.

All CpGs in the map must occur in the methylation input. If the map was created
before probe filtering, explicitly restrict it to the measured probes:

```{r filter-map}
region_map <- region_map[region_map$cpg_id %in% rownames(mvals), , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(region_map) > 0L)
```

# Regional PCs

```{r compute}
res <- compute_regional_pcs(mvals, region_map, pc_method = "gd")
names(res)
res$info
```

The output contains:

| Element | Interpretation |
|:--|:--|
| `regional_pcs` | Retained PCs in rows, samples in columns. |
| `percent_variance` | Within-region variance fractions, one row per PC. |
| `loadings` | Named list of CpG-by-PC data frames, one per region. |
| `info` | Metadata matrix: `region`, `est_dim`, and `num_cpgs`. |

`percent_variance` contains fractions of total within-region variance; multiply
by 100 for percentages. The `info` matrix combines region IDs and counts. The
example below converts its columns to a data frame with explicit column types.

```{r inspect}
res$regional_pcs[, seq_len(4), drop = FALSE]
100 * res$percent_variance
res$loadings[["region-A"]]
info <- data.frame(
    region = as.character(unlist(res$info[, "region"])),
    est_dim = as.integer(unlist(res$info[, "est_dim"])),
    num_cpgs = as.integer(unlist(res$info[, "num_cpgs"]))
)
info
```

Score row names have the form `region-ID-PC1`. Region IDs can themselves contain
hyphens, so split at the final `-PC<number>` suffix if you need separate fields:

```{r score-identifiers}
score_ids <- rownames(res$regional_pcs)
score_key <- data.frame(
    region = sub("-PC[0-9]+$", "", score_ids),
    pc = sub("^.*-(PC[0-9]+)$", "\\1", score_ids)
)
score_key
```

PCA signs are arbitrary: simultaneously reversing a component's scores and
loadings represents the same component. A positive PC score does not by itself
mean higher average methylation. Interpret scores together with the loadings.

# Component selection

`compute_regional_pcs()` defaults to Gavish--Donoho (`"gd"`). Use `"mp"` for
Marchenko--Pastur:

```{r mp}
mp_res <- compute_regional_pcs(mvals, region_map, pc_method = "mp")
mp_res$info
```

Both methods use eigenvalues (`sdev^2`) from `PCAtools::pca()`. CpGs are
centered across samples but are not scaled to unit variance. The noise variance
passed
to both selection methods is fixed at 1. Regional noise is not estimated, and
the threshold does not automatically adjust to a change in input scale.
Beta values and M-values can therefore yield different retained dimensions.

The PCAtools selection routines retain at least one component, including when
no eigenvalue exceeds the threshold. Retention is therefore not a significance
test. The number of CpGs and samples also limits the regional dimension;
a single-CpG region has only one component.

# Array data

The following example uses M-values from `minfiData` and hg19 promoter regions.
It requires additional annotation packages and is not evaluated when this
vignette is built.

```{r array-example, eval=FALSE}
BiocManager::install(c("minfi", "minfiData", "GenomicFeatures",
    "TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene"))
data("MsetEx.sub", package = "minfiData")
array_mvals <- minfi::getM(MsetEx.sub)
gset <- minfi::mapToGenome(MsetEx.sub)
array_cpgs <- GenomicRanges::granges(gset)
txdb <- TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene::TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene
promoters_gr <- GenomicRanges::promoters(GenomicFeatures::genes(txdb),
    upstream = 1000, downstream = 0)
array_map <- create_region_map(array_cpgs, promoters_gr)
array_map <- array_map[
    array_map$cpg_id %in% rownames(array_mvals), , drop = FALSE]
array_res <- compute_regional_pcs(array_mvals, array_map, pc_method = "gd")
```

# Downstream analysis

Transpose `res$regional_pcs` when a downstream model expects samples in rows.
Match phenotype and covariate data to sample IDs explicitly before fitting any
model. Adjust for relevant technical and biological covariates, and account for
multiple testing across the regional components being tested. Regional PCA does
not itself remove confounding or perform differential methylation testing.

```{r sample-oriented-output}
sample_scores <- t(res$regional_pcs)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(sample_scores), colnames(mvals)))
dim(sample_scores)
```

For prediction, PCA should be fitted within the training data. Held-out samples
must use the training centering values and loadings. The package does not
currently provide a separate projection function for new samples.
